cells.tense: The work of growing something is here now, with your own hand steady in it rather than your worry.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Do the next small piece of what you're growing where the person it's for can watch — prune a row, water a pot, hold a seed up to the light.
cells.core:
You've got something growing and you tend it without standing over it. It's coming along because you keep showing up, not because you found the perfect method, and that steady hand lets it arrive at its own pace. People lean on what you've made without ever hearing how you made it, and that quiet is its own kind of ease.

Do one piece of that care where it can be seen this week. Choose the part that was yours anyway — the pruning, the watering, the daily pass — and let someone stand beside it rather than hear about it after. Same hands, same timing. What shifts is that the work has a witness, and setting it down comes easier once it's been seen.

cells.tense: Growing what you tend will have to be enough tomorrow, and the hurry to make tomorrow certain is already in your hands now.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Take ten minutes with something finished and add nothing to it. Sip the cup, sit in the chair, look at the shelf — nothing next, nothing more.
cells.core:
You're trying to write next season into the soil before it grows there. The care is genuine, but it's running ahead of what's actually present, and you can notice it in the grip — watering more than the season calls for here. What you made last time isn't allowed to stand yet because you're already past it, bracing for what comes.

Savour something finished this week. Ten minutes where the job is done, the thing holds, and nothing gets adjusted or carried further. The satisfaction of having imagined and made it is genuine, and it can land now. When a completed thing is allowed to complete, the reach quiets and the next season stops asking to be pre-empted.

cells.tense: The growing happened, and the hand that did it is still standing at a door that has since shut.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Keep a small act you already chose going one more week — same act, even on days it feels pointless — and decide nothing about it yet.
cells.core:
You did the care, and now you've stopped arriving to it. It hasn't gone, exactly; it's back at the door of something already behind you. There's a reach in you that used to go out toward what you grew, and it's pulling inward instead, waiting for a sign that isn't coming.

Carry the chosen version one week further. Not a new plan, not a bigger one — the same small act, done on the days it feels pointless, especially then. You're not asked to feel the care or manufacture the shine. Just hold with it a week more and let understanding catch up in its own time. The light comes back from the work it was pointed at, not from a speech.
cells.sheetLine: The care is still at a door it has already closed behind.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the unforced arrival of what you already are

cells.tense: The care is underway and your own account of it leaves out that it was you.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Leave the shape of what you parted with where the person it was meant for will pass it — the receipt, the empty cup, the rearranged room — and say nothing.
cells.core:
You've been carrying something for someone without naming it, and what you offered up to do that hasn't reached the people it was meant for. The work of tending is doing its job. The account you keep of your own part is thinner than what's actually happening, and the ones being tended to can see the difference, even if you can't.

Let one sacrifice be visible this week. No speech, no ledger — just leave the trace of what you parted with where the person it was meant for will pass it. You don't have to defend it, and the response isn't yours to manage. When what you gave has a witness, release returns as fulfillment rather than a bill you keep paying.

attempts.check: The draft I wrote can sound like the person is already tending someone else's growth at every status; the record only states the mechanism, so a reader could reasonably say nothing is currently in their hands. The ask would still be useful if my read is wrong, because doing the next piece where it can be seen works even when the care is hidden. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one that wants the hidden giving to be gracefully disclosed; I've narrowed it so the act stays with a seed, not with an audience.
